name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus

ethnicAssociations: All ethnicities; lowest in East Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ADA Diagnostic Criteria for Type 1 Diabetes

criteria.description: 2-hour plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) during OGTT
Random plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) with classic hyperglycemic symptoms
Positive islet autoantibodies: anti-GAD65, anti-IA2, anti-ZnT8, anti-insulin (IAA), or anti-ICA
Low or absent C-peptide indicating absolute insulin deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hyperglycemia meeting ADA criteria plus evidence of autoimmune beta-cell destruction (islet autoantibodies) and/or clinical presentation consistent with T1D (acute onset, ketosis-prone, insulin-dependent)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: ADA staging: Stage 1 (2+ autoantibodies, normoglycemia), Stage 2 (2+ autoantibodies, dysglycemia), Stage 3 (clinical diabetes). LADA (latent autoimmune diabetes in adults) presents later with slower progression.

pathognomonic.notes: DKA as initial presentation in ~30% of new diagnoses; characterized by hyperglycemia, ketonemia, metabolic acidosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapid onset of insulin-dependent hyperglycemia with ketosis

rare.notes: Rare but potentially fatal; occurs during DKA treatment
Partial remission with decreased insulin requirements; typically lasts weeks to months after diagnosis

laboratory: Low or absent C-peptide (<0.6 ng/mL; reflects insulin deficiency)
Anti-insulin antibodies (IAA) positive (more common in young children)
Metabolic acidosis (low bicarbonate, low pH) in DKA
imaging: Generally no specific imaging findings for T1D diagnosis
Retinal screening: annual dilated fundoscopy for diabetic retinopathy (starting 5 years after diagnosis)
Abdominal CT if DKA with atypical features (exclude pancreatitis, pancreatic pathology)
other: Screening for associated autoimmune conditions: thyroid (anti-TPO, TSH), celiac (tTG-IgA), adrenal (21-OH antibodies)

redFlags: DKA at presentation (pH <7.3, bicarbonate <18, ketones elevated)
Cerebral edema during DKA treatment (headache, altered consciousness, bradycardia)
Recurrent DKA (consider non-adherence, insulin pump malfunction, eating disorder)
Severe hypoglycemia with loss of consciousness
Signs of associated autoimmune conditions (thyroid disease, celiac, Addison's)
references: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. Classification and Diagnosis of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2024. Diabetes Care. 2024;47(Supplement_1):S20-S42.

Holt RIG, et al. The management of type 1 diabetes in adults. A consensus report by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD). Diabetes Care. 2021;44(11):2589-2625.
Insel RA, et al. Staging presymptomatic type 1 diabetes: a scientific statement of JDRF, the Endocrine Society, and the American Diabetes Association. Diabetes Care. 2015;38(10):1964-1974.
